title: Standard versus ordinary conditions
statement:
Does the standard-state symbol by itself require a temperature of exactly 298.15 K?

[_]{a}

choices: No; the temperature still must be specified.
Yes; the symbol specifies both that temperature and 1 atm.
No; any pressure is automatically standard.
explanations: 298.15 K is the common table choice.
The standard pressure convention is 1 bar and temperature is separate.
The symbol does not specify a temperature.
Standard pressure is a reference condition.

hints: Distinguish standard pressure from table temperature.
298.15 K is common practice, not a built-in temperature.
solution: Standard enthalpy refers to reference states at the stated temperature. Many tables choose 298.15 K, but the standard-state symbol alone does not set temperature.
